verdicts.evidence: 'What do you notice about this writing that makes it high quality? What do you notice about how the sentences start and end?' (Responses will vary, but may include: It has complete sentences. The words explain the pictures. The words are written carefully.)
verdicts.rationale: The lesson partially meets 1.P.EICC.1.d. Students build comprehension and composition repertoire by analyzing two Models of Excellence, noticing and wondering about qualities of high-quality writing ("It has complete sentences. The words explain the pictures"), and co-constructing a High-Quality Work anchor chart with criteria ("includes details," "follows conventions"). Students then draw from these newly built strategies to interpret a second model text during the Back-to-Back and Face-to-Face protocol, where they apply the anchor chart criteria to evaluate Model of Excellence #2 ("The writer told us exactly what each person liked to play with. Each sentence starts with a capital letter."). However, the composition-building clause is only partially met because students identify composition qualities but never actually compose a text in this lesson, and the "draw from skills to construct texts" clause is not met — the teacher states students will use the chart "later in the unit" but no construction occurs here.
